candidates.name: Phil Scott
candidates.bio: Governor of Vermont since 2017 and a former lieutenant governor.

source.title: VTDigger, June 10, 2019: Scott signed H.57 (2019), protecting abortion rights at every stage of pregnancy
source.quote: I have consistently supported a woman's right to choose.

source.title: VTDigger, June 10, 2019: Scott signed H.57 (2019), barring government interference in abortion decisions
Vermont Public, May 22, 2018: Scott vetoed a $15 minimum wage (S.40, 2018), preferring increases tied to inflation
source.quote: more likely to harm those it intends to help

source.title: Vermont Public, May 22, 2018: Scott vetoed a mandatory paid family leave program (H.196, 2018), preferring a voluntary state-run one
Office of Gov. Phil Scott, June 17, 2026: Scott vetoed H.710 (2026), saying it would let industrial wind sites expand with less local scrutiny

candidates.name: Amanda Janoo
candidates.bio: Economist and founder of the Wellbeing Economy Alliance of Vermont, running for statewide office for the first time.

source.title: Vermont Public, March 10, 2026: Janoo's free primary care plan would lay groundwork for a universal health care system
source.quote: ensure free health care for all

source.title: VTDigger, March 10, 2026: Janoo proposes free primary and preventive health care
Vermont Public, March 10, 2026: Janoo would broaden the availability of affordable housing
WCAX, Oct. 8, 2026: Janoo proposes taxing Vermont's highest earners to cut health care and school costs
WCAX primary debate report, July 28, 2026: Janoo would address the roots of repeat offending with a community-first approach
source.quote: the safest communities are the ones where people know their neighbors

source.title: WCAX, Oct. 8, 2026: Janoo would keep small schools open and invest in them, opposing forced mergers

notes.text: Janoo is a first-time candidate with few published positions, and Scott has not released a platform beyond affordability and school consolidation, so many questions are unclear for both.
